bullets.title: COHR: Blowout Q4 FY26 — Revenue $2.05B (+34% YoY), Q1 Guide Above Consensus
bullets.body: Coherent Q4 revenue of $2.05B beat the ~$1.98B consensus and printed at the top of guidance, up 34% YoY (42% pro forma); non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 40.2% and EPS of $1.74 beat the $1.58 estimate (+74% YoY). Q1 guidance of $2.2B–$2.4B (midpoint $2.3B, ~12% QoQ) and EPS $1.85–$2.05 both came in well above the $2.15B/$1.58 consensus; data center and comms now 79% of revenue. Analyst note: Coherent's move into OCS/full systems flagged as a competitive threat to CIEN and CSCO.

bullets.title: CSCO: Q4 FY26 Big Beat — $17.3B Revenue (+18% YoY), Q1 Guide Massively Above Street
bullets.body: Cisco reported Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $1.22 (vs. $1.17 est.) and revenue of $17.3B (+18% YoY, vs. $16.83B est.) with product revenue +24% and non-GAAP operating margin of 35.9%. Q1 guidance of $18.0B–$18.2B revenue (vs. $16.84B consensus) and EPS $1.32–$1.34 (vs. $1.17 est.) were dramatic beats; full-year FY27 EPS guided to $5.05–$5.11 vs. $4.84 expected.

bullets.title: NBIS: Surges 34% (2nd Best Day Ever) While Burry Doubles Down Short in NBIS, MU, ORCL
bullets.body: Nebius (NBIS) soared 34% for its second-best session on record, driven by strong AI infrastructure sentiment following COHR and CoreWeave results. Contrarily, Michael Burry's 13F disclosed he doubled his short in NBIS and added new shorts in Micron (MU) and Oracle (ORCL), plus put options on the SOXX semiconductor ETF — a notable positioning disagreement with the market's bullish momentum.

bullets.title: HOOD: July Monthly Metrics Strong — AUM +19% YoY, Equity Volume +59%, Options +66%
bullets.body: Robinhood reported July 2026 platform metrics: 28.5M funded customers (+1.77M YoY), $355B total AUM (+19% YoY), net deposits of $5.6B (+18% annualized), equity notional volume $333B (+59% YoY), and options contracts of 324M (+66% YoY). All key engagement metrics accelerating.

bullets.title: SNDK: Investor Day Tomorrow at 9am ET; MSCI ACWI Addition Triggers Index Flows
bullets.body: SanDisk is hosting its Investor Day at 9am ET Thursday; previews suggest potential new long-term supply agreements (NBMs) that could set a positive tone for the broader memory sector. Separately, SNDK was named among the three largest additions to the MSCI ACWI index by full market cap, triggering index-fund buying flows.

bullets.title: CART: MSCI ACWI Addition — Among Three Largest by Full Market Cap
bullets.body: Instacart (CART) was named among the three largest additions to the MSCI ACWI index by full market cap in the latest rebalancing (55 additions, 92 deletions), which will trigger passive index-fund inflows at rebalancing.

bullets.title: NVDA: Bullish AI Ecosystem Read-Through; Jensen Huang Tops Glassdoor CEO Rankings
bullets.body: Multiple cross-currents support NVDA: an industry panelist (Eric Vishria) said CSPs, neoclouds, NVIDIA, and chip startups all win in the current AI buildout cycle. COHR's Q4 print — with data center/comms at 79% of revenue and AI capex broadening beyond accelerators — is supplier-level validation of sustained NVDA demand. Jensen Huang was also ranked the #1 CEO of 2026 by Glassdoor.

bullets.title: LITE: Bullish Earnings Sentiment Cited Alongside NBIS as AI Bear Capitulation Signal
bullets.body: LITE was cited alongside NBIS as delivering strong AI-infrastructure earnings that are driving bears to cover shorts. No detailed numbers provided in sourced posts, but the framing is consistent with sector-wide AI infrastructure demand strength.

bullets.title: MU: Burry Adds Short — Bearish 13F Disclosure
bullets.body: Michael Burry's latest 13F shows new/increased short positions in Micron (MU), alongside NBIS and ORCL, and put options on SOXX. No specific thesis detail was provided beyond the position disclosure.

bullets.title: GEV: Funding Milestone for 10 GW Gas Generation Project with US Commerce and Japan
bullets.body: GE Vernova reached a funding milestone on a project to supply up to 10 GW of gas-powered generation capacity, with commercial terms finalized involving the U.S. Department of Commerce and the Government of Japan. No financial terms disclosed.

bullets.title: AAPL: New Siri Impresses; Supplier Call Confirms Pro iPhone Launch This Fall; $9M+ Call Sweep
bullets.body: A tech analyst reports being genuinely impressed with new Siri, noting it automates tasks across supporting apps with capabilities exceeding expectations — though Apple has a perception problem relative to product reality. A supplier earnings call confirmed high-end Pro series phones are still on track for fall launch. Separately, unusual $9M+ call options were detected in AAPL.

bullets.title: INTC: 14A Node Seeing Strong Customer Demand, Partly Capacity-Driven
bullets.body: Analyst commentary notes Intel's 14A process is attracting meaningful customer orders, driven in part by constrained capacity availability elsewhere, as well as performance improvements over prior Intel nodes. Framed as a positive demand signal but with nuance around underlying reasons.

bullets.title: AMD: Highlighting Agentic AI Shifting Compute Infrastructure Requirements
bullets.body: AMD flagged that agentic AI is fundamentally changing compute requirements for AI infrastructure, implying a broadening opportunity set beyond traditional GPU accelerators. Commentary from AMD executive shared by semiconductor industry observer.

bullets.title: SNOW: Hits 52-Week High
bullets.body: Snowflake (SNOW) reached a 52-week high during Wednesday's session, part of a broader group of names hitting new highs alongside JPM and others. No new fundamental catalyst cited.
